plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: Tall, arching plumes of tiny golden flowers light up meadows, roadsides and prairie edges. They hum with bees, butterflies and beetles as summer turns toward autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn, with blooms lasting about 2-4 weeks
plants.location: Meadows and fields across North America
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and carried by insects. The real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time and releases wind-borne pollen.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all the proteas has a bowl-shaped flower head up to 30 cm across. Its petal-like bracts are silky pink and cream, and they surround a crown of fuzzy, pale centre florets. It stands out among the fynbos shrubs on the mountain slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa, including Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its thick, underground stems help it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep through fynbos.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Late winter brings fragrant, fluffy golden pom-poms that cover this small tree and turn southeastern Australian bushland bright yellow. The blooms are bright against the sickle-shaped grey-green foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, typically August and September
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on 1 September, just before this date, to mark the start of spring.
